## Configurations
- Persistence: prediction = HappinessScore at t (validation basis: none (no fitting))
- Linear Regression: OLS, 18 scaled features (validation basis: none (no tuning, fit on train))
- Random Forest: {"n_estimators": 300, "max_depth": 4, "min_samples_leaf": 3, "max_features": 1.0} (validation basis: tuned on validation (optimistic))
- XGBoost: {"n_estimators": 500, "max_depth": 2, "learning_rate": 0.03, "subsample": 0.8, "colsample_bytree": 0.8} (validation basis: tuned on validation (optimistic))
- LSTM: L4_u16: seq_len 4, units [16], dropout 0.1, best epoch 108, seed 42 (validation basis: early stopping + selection on validation (optimistic))
- Stacked Ensemble: LinearRegression meta on [RF, XGB, LSTM] with FIXED-config RF/XGB; weights rf 0.609, xgb 0.082, lstm 0.341, intercept -0.180 (validation basis: 5-fold CV inside validation)

## Lowest test RMSE (descriptive only, one test year, no significance test)
- Lowest overall: Linear Regression (RMSE 0.1238, MAE 0.0938)
- Best of the five fitted models: Linear Regression (RMSE 0.1238, MAE 0.0938); Persistence: RMSE 0.1408, MAE 0.1037
- Linear Regression has a lower test RMSE than Persistence (-12.1%); one test year, so treat the gap with caution.

## Limitations
- Test is a single origin year (2023 -> 2024); differences between models may be within noise.
- Small panel for deep learning; the LSTM used one seed and early stopping on the validation rows.
- Validation numbers of tuned models are optimistic; test numbers are the comparison to cite.
- Stacking meta-model trained on only 133 validation rows with highly correlated base predictions.
- Strict calendar alignment shrinks the training set; Hong Kong and Puerto Rico have no health-expenditure data (flagged, median-imputed).
- Feature importance / weights describe prediction, not causation.
